bibliographic.title: Leveraging chatbots for enhanced decision-making: a comprehensive literature review
bibliographic.citation_apa: Simelane, P. M., & Kittur, J. (2026). Leveraging chatbots for enhanced decision-making: a comprehensive literature review. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 9, 1748544. https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2026.1748544

methodology.sample_description: Thirty-six articles from seven databases reviewed and categorized into six themes
methodology.technology_context: LLM-based chatbots including ChatGPT, GPT-3, and Google Bard used for decision-making and decision support

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed systematic literature review of LLM-based chatbots in decision-making across multiple sectors, with an explicit ethical-considerations theme and human-vs-AI comparison. However, the provided text centers on decision-making quality and user perceptions, not on conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, observability, audit, compliance controls, or structured human oversight frameworks required for central evidence in this review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front-matter and partial introduction text were supplied; full search strategy, screening protocol, quality appraisal, and limitations sections were not available. Extracted year metadata (2023) conflicts with publication citation (2026).

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based only on abstract, keywords, and introductory sections visible in the supplied excerpt. The SLR objective and six-theme framework are clearly stated, but detailed search terms, inclusion/exclusion criteria, quality assessment, and study limitations are not evidenced in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are internally coherent around chatbot-supported decision-making themes, but adequacy and methodological confidence are limited because only partial text was available. Relevance to conversational governance in regulated environments is indirect: ethics and sectoral use are mentioned, but governance, audit, and operational control mechanisms are not evidenced.

axial_codes: ethics and risk in chatbot decisions
coding.subtheme: Benefits, challenges, and ethics across application domains

synthesis.main_claim: LLM-based chatbots such as ChatGPT are increasingly studied as tools for decision-making across sectors, offering personalized recommendations while raising concerns about inconsistent outputs, ethics around sensitive information, and comparison with human decision-making.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a systematic map of chatbot decision-making literature organized into six themes: benefits, challenges, ethical considerations, algorithms/tools, human vs AI decision-making, and applications across fields.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting secondary evidence for background on LLM chatbot deployment and ethical concerns in regulated-adjacent sectors; not suitable as central evidence for conversational governance mechanisms because governance, audit, observability, and compliance controls are not addressed in the supplied text.
